subject: Validate the FD before the user pointer in `timerfd_gettime`
notes:
make format made no changes; make check exited 0 (log at /tmp/commit-f6fYXT-check.log, only warning is rustup's implicit toolchain override notice, not a lint). Both commands run from the worktree with the osdk prefix: PATH=<osdk_bin>:$PATH make check CARGO_OSDK=<osdk_bin>/cargo-osdk. No lint fixes were needed, so no fix round was spent.

Staged the two paths explicitly rather than with `git add -A`. Before staging, `git status --untracked-files=all` showed only these two modified files, and `git status --untracked-files=all test/initramfs/src/regression/` was empty, so no repro file from the diagnose phase survived. After the commit `git status` shows only `?? .osdk/`, which is the harness-installed cargo-osdk toolchain recorded as osdk_bin in state.json (absent from the main repo, not gitignored) -- build infrastructure, not a scratch file, so it was deliberately left untracked and out of the commit.

One commit on top of base e8f2b9ca6, parent confirmed, containing both the kernel change and the pool edit as the repo convention requires. Not pushed, no PR, nothing amended.

Message follows the log's style: imperative subject naming the kernel change with identifiers in backticks, not the test name. Body states the root cause, the invariant and its null-pointer corollary from diagnose.json, and the owning layer (syscall entry layer = the sys_* handler body, since Asterinas has no argument-marshalling layer between the dispatch table and the handler) so a reviewer can judge whether the fix belongs there; it names the rejected wrong-layer alternative (teaching write_val to return EINVAL for address 0). Linux fs/timerfd.c is cited as the reason the precedence is correct, not as the justification on its own. It also records that the fix covers two of ten measured host combinations rather than only the asserted one, and that the two siblings with the same antipattern (sys_timer_gettime, sys_getitimer) were deliberately left alone. gvisor_filter is null, so no per-case blocklist note was needed.
